name: ai.ss33/skill-store
title: SS33 Skill Store
description: Search 60,000 agent skills (SKILL.md procedures) and fetch the one that fits your task.

tools.name: search_skills
tools.description:
Call this BEFORE starting a domain task (a plan, schedule,
procedure, document, configuration or code), even one you know how to do: a
skill may carry specific rules general knowledge will not reproduce. `query`
is a sentence or two describing the task. A candidate with `available`
false is one the store can list but not serve (its licence): get_skill returns
only the author's link. `skill_sets`, when present, lists sets of skills used
together for the whole job, each with its `skill_refs` in order. `area` is the subject area that best fits the
task; skills from that area rank higher (others are still returned). `limit`
1-10 (default 3). Optional `tier` ('frontier' or 'small') for the model that
will follow the skill.

tools.name: get_skill
tools.description:
Fetch a skill's SKILL.md by the `ref` from
search_skills (e.g. "oakoss/vitest-testing-18074849092"). Returns the
markdown to follow. Pass `model` (the model that will use the skill, e.g.
"qwen3.6-27b") or `tier` ("small" for a local / on-device model with a short
context): many skills have a short version written for small models. When
the store holds a skill's supporting files (references, templates, scripts)
they follow the SKILL.md, each under its path; when it does not,
`files_not_stored` is true and `source_url` is the author's folder with them.
A skill whose licence forbids redistribution comes back as an error
(`available` false) with the author's link. To keep a skill for later, save
it as .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md with its files beside it. A ref ending
in @<n> returns version n; a skill set's ref (skill-set/...) returns the set's
steps in order.

tools.name: get_skill_set
tools.description:
Fetch a skill set by the `ref` from
search_skills' `skill_sets` (e.g. "skill-set/patent-drawing-set-179..."): the
skills used together for one job, in order, each with its `ref` for
get_skill, its recommended model size ("frontier" or "small"), its step
label and version. `sequential` true means run the steps in order.

tools.name: report_skill_outcome
tools.description:
After using a skill: did it help with the
task? `notes` says what worked or what was missing or wrong.
